procedure: Stop 0.4.0, replace the `Push_To_GitHub` folder's contents with the candidate's, and click Run.
expected: The add-in starts; the log shows the new version; a backup works (step 3 is that backup).

procedure: Look at the Add-Ins list and the toolbar after K1.
expected: The Add-Ins list shows Push to GitHub; Run works; exactly one Push to GitHub button.

procedure: Open the dialog after the update.
expected: Every repository saved by 0.4.0 is still listed.

procedure: Click Back up now.
expected: The dialog closes when the backup starts; progress messages change and the result appears when it finishes.

procedure: Watch the progress window during the backup.
expected: Progress from the background backup reaches the progress window (custom events arrive on Fusion's main thread).

procedure: Check the backup's files.
expected: Exports are written (exportManager.execute).

procedure: Read the summary.
expected: It names the branch and a short commit id, which match GitHub.

procedure: Look at the repository on GitHub.
expected: The design's files and HISTORY.md are in a folder named after the design; the old root CHANGELOG.md is unchanged.

procedure: Run `git status` and `git log -1` in the local folder before and after the backup.
expected: Both are unchanged by the backup.

procedure: Look in your home folder.
expected: `.fusion_git_repos.json.v0-backup` exists next to `.fusion_git_repos.json` (first upgrade from 0.4.0 or earlier).

procedure: Open the dialog several times; change Files to include several times.
expected: No error ever appears (input ids are reused after deleteMe()).

procedure: Change the files to include.
expected: The Format settings table rebuilds correctly.

procedure: Use the Repository list and Files to include.
expected: Repository selects one item; Files to include allows several.

procedure: Choose another saved repository.
expected: Its saved settings fill in, without extra questions.

procedure: Look at the Repository group.
expected: Edit Repository and Remove Repository are laid out sensibly.

procedure: Open the dialog with a saved repository and an open design.
expected: OK reads Back up now and is greyed out until What changed? is filled in; the line under the files says what is missing and disappears once complete.

procedure: Open the dialog twice.
expected: What changed? is empty every time.

procedure: Look at the toolbar button and Utilities → Add-Ins in light and dark themes, at 100 % and at 150 % or more display scale.
expected: The blue cube with the orange branch is legible everywhere; the same icon is in the Add-Ins list. Screenshots recorded.

procedure: Move the button into the ADD-INS menu, then Stop and Run the add-in and restart Fusion.
expected: It stays in the menu.

procedure: Open Files to include; choose STEP.
expected: Descriptive names ("STEP (.step): for other CAD programs" …); STEP adds no settings row.

procedure: Look at the Design line before and after an unsaved edit.
expected: It shows the name and "Fusion version: vN"; after the edit, "with unsaved changes" and the note about Fusion's own history.

procedure: Change repository, Advanced → Backup branch, and Separate branch per backup.
expected: Saves to changes accordingly.

procedure: Paste an address with a token in it (`https://user:ghp_xxx@github.com/…`).
expected: Refused with an explanation; Back up now stays greyed out.

procedure: Set up a new repository: paste the address, leave Name in this list blank, accept the suggested folder, describe the change, Back up now.
expected: Setup succeeds; the repository is listed under its name from the address.

procedure: At the "This pushes your design to …" notice, answer No.
expected: "Push cancelled — nothing was pushed."; the dialog stays open.

procedure: After F1.
expected: The dialog stays open (executeFailed).

procedure: Back up now again; accept the notice; back up a second time.
expected: The notice appears before the first backup only; both succeed.

procedure: On an account where Git has no name/email: back up; answer No to "all repositories"; back up again.
expected: Asked once; `git config --global user.name` stays unset; not asked again.

procedure: Cancel the name or email prompt.
expected: The backup is cancelled (inputBox).

procedure: Answer Yes/No and Yes/No/Cancel questions during this step.
expected: They behave as their buttons say.

procedure: With the repository from step 5, back up the same design twice.
expected: On GitHub, main has designs/<design>/ with the files and a HISTORY.md listing both backups with Fusion versions; no fusion-export/ branches.

procedure: Set Advanced → Backup branch to fusion-backups and back up.
expected: The branch appears with the design's folder; main doesn't change.

procedure: Back up to the repository saved by 0.4.0 (step 1).
expected: A new fusion-export/... branch per backup; Separate branch per backup is ticked for it.

procedure: After a backup answer Yes; after another, No, then paste the link into the browser.
expected: Yes opens the design's folder on GitHub; No says the link is on the clipboard, and it opens the same folder.

procedure: Check My Setup with a saved repository.
expected: A report with OK lines for Git (and its version), sign-in helper and folder; a GitHub sign-in window if GCM needs one; "GitHub accepted the sign-in…"; nothing pushed; Fusion usable meanwhile.

procedure: Add the test repository again under a second name and folder. Back up a design called Bracket through the first, then a different design also called Bracket through the second.
expected: They land in designs/Bracket/ and designs/Bracket (2)/; the summary explains the second folder.

prerequisites: A repository where you can protect main
procedure: Turn on branch protection for main (GitHub → Settings → Branches) and back up with the running history.
expected: Fails with "…that branch is protected" and suggests a Backup branch.

procedure: Rename the design in Fusion and back up.
expected: It goes to the same folder.

procedure: Back up an unsaved design, save it, back up again.
expected: It keeps its folder after its first save (dataFile.id).

procedure: Back up a different design with the same name.
expected: It goes to Name (2).

procedure: Back up a design named `Arm: v2/final?`.
expected: Folder and files have those characters replaced by _.

procedure: Choose all five file types and back up.
expected: Fusion design, STEP, IGES, SAT and STL are all pushed. If IGES or SAT can't be exported on your Fusion licence, the message says so and nothing is pushed: record it.

procedure: Open the backed-up STEP (and IGES/SAT if made) in another CAD program or viewer.
expected: They open with the expected geometry.

procedure: In the inch design, the 10 mm cube: back up STL and open it in a slicer or viewer.
expected: It is 10 mm (not 0.39 or 254), or the summary says STL files have no units (record the Fusion build).

procedure: STL files → One file per body, with bodies in the root and a component, including two with the same name.
expected: One file per body, named <design> - <component path> - <body>.stl, each in the right position relative to the others.

procedure: Hide a body; back up per body.
expected: Hidden bodies are skipped with a warning.

procedure: Make an export fail (for example an empty design with STL chosen).
expected: "Nothing was pushed because these exports failed"; GitHub unchanged; the dialog stays open.

procedure: Insert the second design as a linked component, choose Fusion design and back up; answer No, then repeat and answer Yes.
expected: The question names the linked component; No pushes nothing; Yes pushes <design>.f3z (not .f3z.f3d) and HISTORY.md has the linked-components note. If the summary says Fusion couldn't write an .f3z, record the technical details.

procedure: Include a nested linked component and a broken link (a linked design you moved or deleted).
expected: Both are detected or reported; nothing crashes.

procedure: Download that .f3z (or .f3d) and open it in Fusion, ideally in a project or account without the linked design.
expected: Record whether the linked component's geometry is present and whether the linked design came with it. This decides the warning's wording and R-06.

procedure: During a long backup, orbit the view and open a menu.
expected: Fusion stays usable; progress keeps changing.

procedure: Start a second backup while one runs.
expected: Refused with an explanation; the first completes.

procedure: Cancel before the backup reaches GitHub.
expected: "nothing was pushed"; no new commit or branch on GitHub.

procedure: Cancel after a question has hidden and re-shown the progress window.
expected: Cancel works (wasCancelled).

procedure: Cancel just after GitHub accepted the backup (large export).
expected: The message says it did reach GitHub, naming the branch.

procedure: With separate branches, use Use this branch instead with an existing branch.
expected: The question appears on top; the backup continues after the answer.

procedure: Watch questions and messages during background backups.
expected: They appear on top, not behind the progress window.

procedure: As H15.
expected: The progress window hides for questions and comes back.

procedure: Close the design's document during a backup.
expected: The backup finishes or fails cleanly; Fusion doesn't crash.

procedure: Advanced → Manage Token… → Yes.
expected: The Token field shows dots.

procedure: As D1.
expected: isPassword works in this Fusion build.

procedure: Save Token.
expected: Confirmed; Use stored token ticked; the field is empty.

procedure: Back up with the stored token.
expected: It succeeds.

procedure: Right after D3, look in %LOCALAPPDATA%\PushToGitHub\credentials.
expected: It is empty (the per-command credential folder was removed).

procedure: `git config --local http.proxy http://127.0.0.1:9` in the local folder, back up with the token, then unset it.
expected: Refused before anything is sent, naming http.proxy.

procedure: `git config --local remote.origin.pushurl https://github.com/<you>/<another-repo>.git`, back up with the token, then unset it.
expected: Refused ("would send the push to …").

procedure: Edit Repository… → rename → Save Changes.
expected: The list shows the new name; the stored token still works.

procedure: Manage Token… → Replace, then → Delete.
expected: Both work.

procedure: Help & Privacy → Open Log File…; search it for the start of your token.
expected: The log opens and contains no token.

procedure: Clear Log; Privacy Policy….
expected: The log is deleted; PRIVACY.md opens in the browser.

procedure: Edit → change the address → No to updating the local folder.
expected: The folder's Git remote is unchanged.

procedure: Edit → change the address to a different server.
expected: Use stored token is turned off, with an explanation.

procedure: Remove Repository… → confirm.
expected: The entry disappears; the local folder remains; a stored token is kept unless you said Yes to deleting it.

procedure: Disconnect the network, then back up.
expected: A readable error ("Couldn't reach GitHub.") within a few minutes; Fusion recovers.

procedure: Start a large backup, then disconnect the network while it is sending.
expected: It fails with a readable message within the time limit (or reports it couldn't tell whether it arrived); Fusion stays responsive; reconnect and back up again succeeds.

procedure: Read the network failure message from F2.
expected: It starts "Couldn't reach GitHub." with Git's text under Technical details. No dialog in the whole campaign shows a Python traceback.

procedure: Start a backup and Stop the add-in during it.
expected: Fusion doesn't hang; Run again works and shows one button.

procedure: Stop and Run five times.
expected: Exactly one button each time; backups work after the last Run.

procedure: Covered by K4 (at least three cycles).
expected: As K4.

procedure: Stop then Run.
expected: No second button (addCommand with an existing id).

procedure: Stop, bring back the 0.4.0 files and the .v0-backup settings (docs/INSTALL.md → Go back), Run; then Stop, put the candidate and your settings back, Run.
expected: 0.4.0 starts and works in the same session; then the candidate starts again.

procedure: Copy the add-in folder to Push_To_GitHub_copy and Run it.

procedure: Use the other add-ins you normally run.

procedure: End Fusion from Task Manager while the add-in runs, then start Fusion.
expected: Exactly one button; the add-in works.

procedure: Choose or set up a repository folder inside OneDrive or Dropbox.

expected: No note.

procedure: After the restart.

procedure: After the restart.

procedure: Open the dialog; then quit, put your settings file back, start Fusion.
expected: A message names the .corrupt-… copy; after restoring, the repositories are listed.
